steps.name: Load, QC, and prepare paired count matrix
caveats: Verify gene symbol column name and sample column naming convention against metadata subject/condition labels before assuming order
Do not drop the subject identifier — it is required for the paired design in the next step
steps.question: Do the counts.csv (12000 genes x 10 samples + gene symbol column) and metadata.csv (10 samples: subject, condition) form a valid paired design with 5 subjects each having one control and one treated sample, and which genes pass a minimal expression filter for paired DESeq2 modeling?
constraints: Do not perform any differential expression testing in this step — QC and filtering only
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix loaded with genes as rows, 10 sample columns matching metadata sample identifiers exactly
Metadata confirmed to have exactly 5 unique subjects, each with exactly one control and one treated sample (condition column)
Low-count genes filtered (e.g. require count >0 in a minimum number of samples) prior to DESeq2, with the number of genes retained reported
Sample order in count matrix programmatically matched/reordered to metadata rows before DE modeling

steps.name: Paired DESeq2 differential expression (treated vs control, blocked on subject)
caveats: With n=5 pairs, statistical power is limited — report this explicitly rather than overinterpreting genes near the significance threshold
Confirm condition is coded consistently (e.g. treated vs control) so fold-change direction is biologically interpretable
This is a paired/blocked design (~subject + condition), not a naive two-group comparison — using an unpaired model here would ignore the subject structure the research question depends on
steps.question: Within each of the 5 subjects, which genes are significantly differentially expressed between the treated and control blood samples, using a paired design (~subject + condition) in DESeq2 on the filtered raw counts?
constraints: Use raw integer counts as DESeq2 input, not pre-normalized values
Report both nominal and BH-adjusted p-values
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 (or pydeseq2) run with design formula including subject and condition terms (paired/blocked design), condition being control vs treated
Full results table produced with log2 fold change, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value for every retained gene
Significant gene list reported at a stated adjusted p-value threshold (e.g. padj < 0.05), with counts of up- and down-regulated genes
Independent filtering / outlier handling defaults documented; results table saved as an artifact for downstream enrichment

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-responsive genes
caveats: Gene symbols in the GMT are HGNC; confirm the DE gene identifiers match this symbol space before matching (no case/alias mismatches)
With only 12000 background genes profiled, use the profiled gene set (not a genome-wide background) as the enrichment background where the test supports it
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among the genes identified as significantly differentially expressed between treated and control blood samples across the 5 paired subjects?
constraints: Report the WikiPathways snapshot version (2026.07.10) used for reproducibility
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g. over-representation or GSEA-style ranked test) run on the significant DE gene list (and/or full ranked gene list by test statistic) from T1S2
Uses the human WikiPathways gene set collection confirmed present in the reference store
Enrichment results table reports pathway name, gene set size, overlap genes, p-value and adjusted p-value
If the significant gene list from T1S2 is empty or very small, report that explicitly rather than forcing enrichment on an inadequate list

plan.title: Paired subject-level DE of treatment vs control blood
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 5 subjects, each contributing a paired control and treated blood sample (10 samples, paired by subject), with raw STAR/featureCounts integer gene-level counts (12000 genes x 11 columns incl. gene symbol). This paired structure means subject-to-subject variability can and should be modeled directly rather than treating samples as independent groups. The plan: (1) load and QC the counts/metadata, confirm the pairing structure and filter low-count genes; (2) run a paired differential expression analysis in DESeq2 using a subject + condition design (a paired model) to identify genes that respond to treatment across subjects, which directly answers the stated research question of genes responding to treatment while accounting for subject-level pairing; (3) functionally characterize the resulting DE gene list against human WikiPathways gene sets to translate the statistical result into pathway-level biology, since the reference census confirms a human WikiPathways GMT is available. Steps are sequenced as a linear DAG: QC/prep -> paired DE -> pathway enrichment.
